subject: EVALUATE statement
notes: kb/Work PB398 - LANDED, and kb/Work PB594 RE-VERDICTED on top of it. The phrase exists (valueRange gains `(IN cobolWord)?`, measured off the printed page PDF p649 / folio 619: the bracket follows the right-hand operand brace, IN is un-underlined and alphabet-name-1 is required inside it) and BOTH sentences of SR3 are enforced at the ONE site 14.7.8's opening sentence asks for, shared by the EVALUATE and the VALUE clause. ### PB594's re-measurement (wave 43 group D): PB594 measured `EVALUATE W-X WHEN "A" THRU "F" IN ALPHA-1` as `COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'IN'` plus a four-diagnostic cascade that lost the rest of the EVALUATE. RE-PROBED at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 on the wave-43 build: it parses and runs, so PB594 is DISCHARGED - the landing that fixed it was PB398 (2573338ec, `git log -S` on the rule body). THE NOTE'S REAL BAR WAS THE SEMANTIC HALF, NOT THE PARSE - 'otherwise the phrase parses and is silently ignored, which is the worse defect' - and it is met in both directions, measured: SR3's screen refuses a NUMERIC range under an alphabet by name (COBOL1998, negative/pb398-range-alphabet-numeric-operands), and the named alphabet actually DECIDES the comparison - over `ALPHABET ALPHA-2 IS "C" "B" "A" "F" "E" "D"`, `WHEN "A" THRU "F" IN ALPHA-2` answers OUT for "B" while the same range with no phrase answers IN, at every edition. ### EVIDENCE-UNION REPAIR (wave 43 group E): batch-03 of this group re-recorded the row with only two of its five test-refs and one of its seven code-locations, and misspelled `negative/pb398-range-alphabet-numeric-operands` as `negative/pb398-range-alphabet-numeric` - a reference to a case that does not exist. record_verdicts.py REPLACES a row's evidence fields rather than merging them and does not check that a `conformance:` ref resolves, so a batch written to ADD evidence silently subtracted it. This record restores the union; the dangling ref was the ONLY one in all 3,821 conformance refs in the inventory (swept). kb/Work PB843 (wave 45 finisher): the rule's IDENTIFIER arm ('the literals or identifiers specified in the THROUGH phrase') was unreachable - over identifier-4 the greedy qualification loop took `IN alphabet-name-1` as a qualifier and the verdict was COBOL1639 on 'WS-HIINAL'. EvaluateBinder.BindRangeHigh now re-reads a LAST `IN word` naming a declared alphabet as the phrase (8.3.2.2: a word is only one type of user-defined word, so an alphabet-name is never a qualifier) and binds the reference without it; SR3's class screens then run over identifiers too (negative pb843-range-identifier-alphabet-numeric -> COBOL1998).
